OpenShift services that run on the control planeComponentDescriptionOpenShift API serverThe OpenShift API server validates and configures the data forOpenShift resources, such as projects, routes, and templates.The OpenShift API server is managed by the OpenShift API ServerOperator.OpenShift controller managerThe OpenShift controller manager watches etcd for changes toOpenShift objects, such as project, route, and template controllerobjects, and then uses the API to enforce the specified state.The OpenShift controller manager is managed by the OpenShiftController Manager Operator.OpenShift OAuth API serverThe OpenShift OAuth API server validates and configures the data toauthenticate to OpenShift Container Platform, such as users, groups,and OAuth tokens.The OpenShift OAuth API server is managed by the ClusterAuthentication Operator.OpenShift OAuth serverUsers request tokens from the OpenShift OAuth server to authenticatethemselves to the API.The OpenShift OAuth server is managed by the Cluster AuthenticationOperator.Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticOpenShift Container Platform 4.12 Architecture3' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '4' (X=0.00). OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on ' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their p' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'u' (X=0.00). For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are ma' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'n' (X=0.00). OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with ' ' (X=0.00). They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), ' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are ins' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 't' (X=0.00). Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefaul' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to pe' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'r' (X=0.00). These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optio' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'n' (X=0.00). You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, ' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by ' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'O' (X=0.00). Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operato' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'r' (X=0.00). Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible ' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'f' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for use' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'r' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to r' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'u' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in t' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'h' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00

OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their ap' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with 'p' (X=0.00). They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. Cluster OperatorsIn OpenShift Container Platform, all cluster functions are divided' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with ' ' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00

You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. Cluster OperatorsIn OpenShift Container Platform, all cluster functions are divided into a' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
DEBUG: Merging 'Some of these services on the control plane machines run as systemd services, while others run as staticpods.Systemd services are appropriate for services that you need to always come up on that particularsystem shortly after it starts. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. For control plane machines, those include sshd, which allows remote login.It also includes services such as:The CRI-O container engine (crio), which runs and manages the containers. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. OpenShiftContainer Platform 4.12 uses CRI-O instead of the Docker Container Engine.Kubelet (kubelet), which accepts requests for managing containers on the machine from controlplane services.CRI-O and Kubelet must run directly on the host as systemd services because they need to be runningbefore you can run other containers.The installer-* and revision-pruner-* control plane pods must run with root permissions because theywrite to the /etc/kubernetes directory, which is owned by the root user. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. These pods are in the followingnamespaces:openshift-etcdopenshift-kube-apiserveropenshift-kube-controller-manageropenshift-kube-scheduler6.3. OPERATORS IN OPENSHIFT CONTAINER PLATFORMOperators are among the most important components of OpenShift Container Platform. Operators arethe preferred method of packaging, deploying, and managing services on the control plane. They canalso provide advantages to applications that users run.Operators integrate with Kubernetes APIs and CLI tools such as kubectl and oc commands. Theyprovide the means of monitoring applications, performing health checks, managing over-the-air (OTA)updates, and ensuring that applications remain in your specified state.Operators also offer a more granular configuration experience. You configure each component bymodifying the API that the Operator exposes instead of modifying a global configuration file.Because CRI-O and the Kubelet run on every node, almost every other cluster function can be managedon the control plane by using Operators. Components that are added to the control plane by usingOperators include critical networking and credential services.While both follow similar Operator concepts and goals, Operators in OpenShift Container Platform aremanaged by two different systems, depending on their purpose:Cluster Operators, which are managed by the Cluster Version Operator (CVO), are installed bydefault to perform cluster functions.Optional add-on Operators, which are managed by Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM), can bemade accessible for users to run in their applications.6.3.1. Cluster OperatorsIn OpenShift Container Platform, all cluster functions are divided into a series of default clusterCHAPTER' (X=0.00, W=0.00) with '' (X=0.00). Gap=0.00. Threshold=2.00, Wide=30.00
